Question_text: A student performs an experiment to measure an elastic property of wood. (a) A metre rule is clamped with its 10.0cm mark at the edge of a bench, as shown in Fig. 1.1. ho = 75.5 cm
image: Fig. 1.1 shows a diagram of a metre rule clamped at the 10.0 cm mark to the edge of a bench. The free end of the rule extends over the bench. A vertical dashed line indicates the height `h0` from the floor to the free end, labeled as 75.5 cm.

Parts.part_text: On Fig. 1.1, draw a second rule positioned to measure the height `h0` above the floor of the free end of the clamped metre rule.
On Fig. 1.1, draw the position of the eye of the student when measuring `h0`.

A mass m is hung from the 95.0cm mark on the clamped metre rule, as shown in Fig. 1.2. The end of the rule moves down a distance d, where d = `h0` – h. The student takes readings of h for different values of m. Values of m and h are recorded in the table of Fig. 1.3.
Parts.image: Fig. 1.2 shows the same setup as Fig. 1.1, but with an additional mass `m` hanging from the metre rule at the 95.0 cm mark. The rule is shown bent downwards. A vertical dashed line from the floor to the deflected end of the rule is labeled `h`. Another vertical dashed line from the floor to the original position of the free end is labeled `h0`, with `h0 = 75.5 cm`. A small `d` is indicated between `h` and `h0`, representing the deflection.

Parts.part_text: Complete Fig. 1.3 to show the values of d.
On Fig. 1.4, plot the graph of d/cm on the y-axis against m/g on the x-axis. Start your graph from the origin and draw the straight line of best fit.
Parts.image: Fig. 1.4 is a large empty grid with horizontal and vertical axes, clearly marked for plotting a graph of `d/cm` against `m/g`.

Parts.part_text: Explain how the graph shows that d is not directly proportional to m.
Find the gradient of your graph. Show your working clearly.
Use information from (b) to find the length L along the clamped metre rule from the edge of the bench to the point where the hanging mass is attached.
The elastic property E of the wood is given by the relationship E = (0.72 x L^3) / gradient Calculate the value of E. You do not need to give the unit of your answer.

Question_text: A group of students measures the speed of a wave along a slinky spring. A teacher and a student hold the ends of a slinky spring stretched along a bench, as shown in Fig. 2.1. The teacher moves one end of the spring to make a wave pulse travel along the spring. Five metre rules are placed end-to-end alongside the spring. Five students with stopwatches stand together near the centre of the spring to measure the time t taken by the wave pulse to travel the distance of 5.0 m.
image: Fig. 2.1 shows a long slinky spring stretched horizontally on a bench. A teacher stands at one end, and a student at the other, holding the spring ends. Five metre rules are laid end-to-end along the length of the spring. Five other students are standing along the length of the spring, each with a stopwatch, observing the wave travel.

Parts.part_text: The five students record the following values for t, measured in seconds. 1.71 1.64 1.78 1.75 1.67
Find the average time `t_av` for the wave to travel 5.0m along the spring.
Calculate the average speed `v_av` of the wave pulse along the spring. Give your answer to a suitable number of significant figures.
Explain why, in practice, the position of the students and the metre rules causes a parallax error.
Explain why this parallax error causes the measured values of t to be too small.
Explain one other reason why the times recorded by the students are not all exactly the same.
Describe how the students could measure the time t more accurately.
One student suggests that the speed of a slower wave pulse can be measured more accurately. Suggest a method of making a wave pulse travel more slowly along the spring.

image: Fig. 3.1 shows a drawing of a thermistor, which is a bulb-shaped component with two leads, labeled 'thermistor'. Adjacent to it, its circuit symbol is shown, which is a resistor symbol with a diagonal line through it, labeled 'circuit symbol'.

Parts.part_text: In the space below, draw the circuit diagram of a circuit used to measure the resistance of the thermistor.
Explain, with the aid of a diagram, how the temperature of the thermistor may be measured and varied from room temperature to 90°C.

A student measures the resistance of the thermistor at different temperatures and plots a graph of resistance against temperature. Explain why the resistance must be measured at more than two different temperatures.

Question_text: A student investigates pressure using a pencil and two blocks of modelling clay. The pencil is pushed gently into the clay. The pencil leaves a dent. The flat end of the pencil is used first and then the pointed end. This is shown in Fig. 4.1.
image: Fig. 4.1 displays two side-by-side scenarios. In the left scenario, a pencil is shown with its flat eraser end being pushed downwards into a block of modelling clay, creating a shallow, wide dent. In the right scenario, the same pencil is shown with its pointed lead end being pushed downwards into another block of modelling clay, creating a narrow, deep dent. Both scenarios are labeled with 'push', 'pencil', and 'modelling clay'.

Parts.part_text: Describe a simple method for pushing the pencil gently into the clay with the same force each time. You may use a diagram in your answer.
On Fig. 4.1, draw the side view of the dent produced in each piece of clay when the pencil is pushed gently into the clay with the same force each time.
